## Why This Is Asked
This question probes practical debugging under latency budgets, demanding familiarity with CPU frequency scaling, turbo dynamics, and CPU isolation in production Linux setups.

## Key Concepts
- CPU frequency scaling and turbo boost behavior
- CPU governors and performance vs. power trade-offs
- Thread pinning (sched_affinity) and CPU isolation (isolcpus)
- Observability using simple, widely available tools

## Code Example
```bash
# Simple live freq sampling across all CPUs
while true; do echo -n "$(date +%s)"; for c in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/cpuinfo_cur_freq; do echo -n "  $((1000#$c)):"; cat $c; done; echo; sleep 0.5; done
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you automate detection and mitigation across multiple hosts?
- What are NUMA implications when isolating CPUs on a multi-socket system?

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses hands-on Linux troubleshooting for latency with containerized workloads, focusing on memory reclamation, THP behavior, and safe, minimal-impact mitigations.

- Transparent Huge Pages (THP) behavior and toggling

- Default tooling for on-call debugging

## Code Example
```bash
# Check THP state
cat /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled
# Observe memory/caching behavior

# Disk and I/O detail

# Identify running containers

# See heavy processes inside a container

# Mitigation: disable THP and pin a pid to CPUs
sudo tee /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled <<< 'never'
taskset -cp 0-7 <pid>
```

## Why This Question Matters
This tests advanced multi-tenant Linux isolation skills, validating the ability to map processes to cgroups, quantify per-cgroup memory pressure, and apply safe limits without impacting other tenants.

## Key Concepts

### 1. cgroup Version Detection
Determine whether the system uses cgroup v1 (hierarchical, separate controllers) or cgroup v2 (unified hierarchy).
- v1 path: `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/<cgroup>/`
- v2 path: `/sys/fs/cgroup/<cgroup>/`

### 2. Process-to-cgroup Mapping
- `/proc/[pid]/cgroup` reveals which cgroup owns each process
- `systemd-cgtop` provides real-time per-cgroup resource metrics
- Critical for identifying which tenants are affected

### 3. Memory Pressure Indicators
- `memory.usage_in_bytes` / `memory.current` approaching `memory.limit_in_bytes` / `memory.max`
- Elevated `pgpgin`, `pgfault` in `memory.stat`
- Swap activity (si/so in `vmstat`) when memory is constrained

### 4. Mitigation Strategy
- Set `memory.limit_in_bytes` (v1) or `memory.max` (v2) to cap memory per cgroup
- Use `memory.swappiness` (v1) or `memory.swap.max` (v2) to control swap behavior
- Always verify limits post-application to ensure they took effect
- Monitor to confirm latency normalizes after limits are applied
